page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes a 50 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets, though it lacks newer extensions like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 262 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates that the E16s_v3 delivers average multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. In stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU tests, the instance scores in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also fall within the average range. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression tests ranking in the bottom 25% tier. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are average, but prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16s_v3 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-threaded CPU performance. The combination of 128.0 GB of RAM, Premium Storage compatibility, and average database operation benchmarks makes this instance suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and general enterprise applications requiring a high memory footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure E16s_v3 is an ESv3-family memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it includes 262 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though single-core performance and compression tasks fall into the bottom 25% tier. Lacking GPU acceleration, this instance relies on its high memory density and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise application servers that benefit from high memory capacity but do not demand high single-threaded compute performance.
